text:
Marta: heads-up — i've been prototyping a small change to the ts-sdk to emit a `quota-hint` header for requests so the console can surface per-route quota allocation. thinking out loud: should this be opt-in by default? :thinking:

Ryan: curious — what's in the header exactly? examples?

Marta: simple JSON-ish string for now, e.g. `quota-hint=route=/chat/transform,priority=low`

Anya: fwiw if we start sending route names we risk exploding cardinality in the telemetry tables. we should never send raw route strings.

Ben: agree with Anya. alternative: send a stable, short route hash + a mapping table uploaded from the console/operator side. e.g. `quota-hint=route_hash:3f7a2b,prio:L`

Sahil: +1 on hashing. also we should add sampling so we don't double-bill metrics. propose two flags in the sdk config: `quotaHints: {enabled: boolean, sampleRate: 0.01}` and `routeMapUpload: <console-token>`

Marta: sample idea: SDK will send header only for 1% of requests by default and attach `X-Quota-Sampled: 1` when included. console aggregates sampled signals to estimate distribution.

Ryan: concerns: proxies & CDNs might strip custom headers. can we put it in structured metadata that survives? e.g., body metadata or an auth-signed token?

Anya: signed token is heavy for most clients. body metadata changes request shapes and could break gateways. headers are simplest but we should document fallback. maybe include an opt-in that uses query param for GETs (ugly tho).

Ben: another angle — do we want this tied to quota accounting or purely observability? mixing the two can make rollouts scary. if quota decisions will ever depend on it we need stricter guarantees.

Marta: good call. current plan is observability-first. quota engine will continue to use committed capacity/route id from server-side routing. header is just a hint to help mapping usage in console UX and to suggest per-route quota recommendations in Optimize.

Sahil: UX ask: the console should display both sampled estimate and sample size, plus a confidence band. otherwise customers will freak out when numbers aren't exact.

Marta: agreed — i'll flesh out a small console wireframe. question for devex: default opt-in? opt-out?

Ryan: make it opt-in for GA. we can enable an org-level toggle in console and expose a telemetry-opt-in key to SDKs. start opt-in for safety.

Anya: and add automatic scrubbing: if route names ever appear in header, sdk should hash them client-side before transmission.

Ben: technical note: add a short TTL for route-hash mappings in the console so stale names don't accumulate. maybe a weekly GC job based on last-seen timestamps.

Marta: plan of action: 1) PR to ts-sdk adding `quotaHints` opt-in with sampling + client-side hashing 2) console feature flag + mapping ingestion endpoint 3) wireframe for sampled metric panel 4) rollout doc with telemetry cardinality mitigation. i'll draft the PR and design doc tomorrow.

deploy-bot: scheduled deploy to staging for sdk branch `feat/quota-hints` at 2028-08-04T15:00:00Z (:rocket:)

Sahil: thanks — i'll review the console side once the wireframe lands.

Ryan: thanks all. quick follow-up: can we add a tiny example snippet for the ts-sdk in the PR description? makes adoption easier.

Marta: yes — will include a snippet and a note about proxies and fallback.

Anya: tagging retention: please add an issue to track telemetry cardinality tests before enabling org-wide.

Marta: added to my todo list. :+1:
